portraits.riya: A nineteen-year-old Indian college student, bright alert eyes, messy bun, oversized hoodie, headphones round her neck, lit by a laptop screen in a dark hostel room, warm and full of mischief
portraits.zoya: An Indian woman of twenty-eight in plain clothes police attire, sharp tired eyes, hair tied back, a paper chai cup in hand, fluorescent office light, unsentimental
portraits.dev: An Indian man of twenty-one, soft features, red-rimmed eyes, hooded sweatshirt, sitting in a parked car at night, guilt written across his face

scenes.2am: A cramped video-editing studio at 2 AM in an Indian city: two monitors glowing on a timeline, cold blue light, a phone face-up on the desk screen lit with an incoming call, cigarette smoke haze, dead marigold garland on the wall
scenes.before-midnight: The same studio the next night, monitors dark, only a desk lamp: a small muddy paper note unfolded beside the phone, a chai glass gone cold, rain on the window
scenes.diwali-night: The same studio during Diwali: fireworks flashing green and gold through the window blinds, the room strobing, the phone glowing on the desk, strings of lights on the building opposite
scenes.1158: The same studio at 11:58 PM, fireworks finished, only smoke drifting past the window, the phone screen the single light source, the chair pushed back and empty

cover: A phone lying face-up on a dark editing desk at 2 AM, its screen a plain glowing blank rectangle with a single small purple heart shape and two round call buttons — absolutely no letters, no numbers, no words anywhere in the image — marigold petals scattered on the desk, cold blue monitor light, Diwali fireworks blurred through the window behind, ominous and intimate
ambient: Late-night Indian city interior: distant traffic hum, a ceiling fan turning, faint far-off Diwali firecrackers, the electrical whine of monitors, an occasional dog barking blocks away. Seamless loop, no melody, no voices.
